8gb of ram, and is this being shared with the graphics processing? What is your split like? Specifically how much of that 8 is being used by the APU?

VRchat is an interesting game to consider optimizations for. For a regular game there are always levels of detail on models and textures, and the engine can show crappier textures and models. 

At some point VRChat is going to start using the streaming mip maps they ask for with avatar uploads, so instead of requiring the full VRAM hit, it's only loading so much.

With all of the content being user generated, and how heavy most avatars are, I don't think VRChat themselves can do much. Windows 10 recent versions probably take a bit more ram than the initial versions. Graphics drivers get slowly bigger and bigger. 

If you could run VRChat without the overhead of any operating system you might be fine with the 6gb of ram you're actually getting.

I'm pretty sure VRChat is using 16gb of ram on my computer
Maybe people being able to run the mobile or the quest version on a PC would solve the low-end PC hardware problem

details:
Dear VRChat development team,

nowadays, whenever I try to run VRChat on my Windows 10 laptop that uses AMD A9, 8 GB RAM, and a storage of 237 GB, it would usually have issues such as, avatars on other people and myself not loading, sometimes showing up as an error bot, the frame rate sometimes decreasing when I'm in a world for a while, and worlds with small sizes taking a very long time to load and sometimes ending up taking me to my home world instead. But it wasn't like this during Mid 2019 to mid 2021, When I was on my early days of playing VRChat during 2019, I played on a small laptop that had a 2-digit amount of Gigabytes of storage, somewhere around 80, and it performed very decently, it could load avatars very well, had a high frame rate and only issue was that it couldn't load big worlds. During the same year I got a new laptop which was bigger and had more storage and it could load bigger worlds and the performance was still decent, it was pretty much the same, only difference is that I could load in bigger worlds with that laptop, and it would stay like that for a long time whenever I would open VRChat on desktop. That laptop then broke during April 2022 so I couldn't play VRChat on desktop so I don't really know how the performance was during most of that year. But when I got a new laptop in during late 2022 and I tried opening up VRChat, It performed well with loading avatars and worlds but however, somewhere around 3 or more months later, It started to not perform as well as how it did during the first few weeks when I got my new laptop, and that leads to the performance issues I have today when I try running VRChat on my laptop.

The worst part is that I don't know exactly what's causing these issues, I tried clearing both content and avatar cache, uninstalling and reinstalling, restarting my laptop, and adjusting the in-game performance settings. But none of that worked. I'm not sure if it's the updates or that the system requirements are being raised, or Easy Anti-Cheat, and I am quite concerned about it, it gives me a feeling that VRChat is gradually becoming more and more expensive to access, and the problem is  not everyone can afford fancy gaming PCs with RTX or GeForce GTX.

VRChat shouldn't be this luxurious world for people who have expensive PCs, it should be an accessible free social platform for people who want to socially interact with other people and explore worlds.

In conclusion, optimization for low-end PCs and laptops seriously needs to be taken into account.
title: Perfomance on low-end pcs and laptops seriously needs improvement.
